text.en: Which open-source framework is commonly used to write unit tests in T-SQL?

explanation.en: tSQLt lets you write tests as stored procedures with fakes and assertions, each running in a rolled-back transaction. Selenium is UI testing; JMeter is load testing.

example.en: EXEC tSQLt.Run 'OrderTests';

text.en: In a tSQLt unit test, why use tSQLt.FakeTable on dbo.OrderLines?
To replace the table with an empty, constraint-free copy so the test controls its data in isolation

explanation.en: FakeTable isolates the test from existing data and constraints; changes roll back after the test. It doesn't affect production or permanently drop anything.

example.en: EXEC tSQLt.FakeTable 'dbo.OrderLines'; INSERT test rows; assert.

text.en: What distinguishes an integration test from a unit test for database code?
Integration tests exercise the deployed schema end-to-end (constraints, triggers, multiple objects, app access) against a real database
Integration tests never use a database
Unit tests always run in production

explanation.en: Unit tests isolate one object; integration tests validate how objects (and apps) work together after deployment.

example.en: Deploy the dacpac to a container, run API tests that insert orders and read through RLS.

text.en: Before deploying, you want to know whether anyone changed production's schema outside the pipeline since the last deployment. Which SqlPackage action?

explanation.en: DriftReport lists changes to a registered database since its last deployment. Export/Import handle bacpacs; Extract creates a dacpac.

example.en: sqlpackage /Action:DriftReport /TargetConnectionString:"…" /OutputPath:drift.xml

text.en: Every PR touching /src/Database must be approved by the DBA team. What enforces this in GitHub?
A CODEOWNERS entry for /src/Database/ plus branch protection requiring Code Owner review

explanation.en: CODEOWNERS maps paths to owners and, with 'Require review from Code Owners', makes their approval mandatory. Notes and labels don't enforce anything.

example.en: /src/Database/ @contoso/dba-team

text.en: Production deployments must wait for a manual approval by release managers. Which GitHub feature implements this?
An environment with required reviewers that the deploy job targets

explanation.en: Environment protection rules pause jobs until listed reviewers approve; wait timers and branch restrictions add further control.

example.en: jobs.deploy.environment: production (Settings → Environments → Required reviewers)

text.en: Order a typical database CI/CD pipeline.
Build the SQL project and run unit tests (CI on PR)
Deploy to test and run integration tests
Approval gate, then deploy the same dacpac to production

explanation.en: Validate early, produce one artifact, test it deployed, then promote it with approval.

example.en: Build once, deploy many.

text.en: For each statement about branch protection on main, answer Yes or No.
It can require pull requests before merging.
It can require specific status checks (CI jobs) to pass.
It can require approval from code owners.

explanation.en: Branch protection/rulesets govern how changes enter a branch; deployment is done by workflows and environments.

example.en: Combine with environment approvals for full control from commit to production.

text.en: Which GitHub Action is designed to deploy SQL projects or dacpacs to Azure SQL?

explanation.en: azure/sql-action builds .sqlproj files or deploys .dacpac/.sql to Azure SQL. The others cache dependencies, label PRs or run code scanning.

example.en: with: { path: ./Sales.dacpac, action: publish, arguments: /Profile:prod.publish.xml }

text.en: Why promote the SAME dacpac from test to production instead of rebuilding for each environment?
Production then receives exactly the artifact that passed testing

explanation.en: 'Build once, deploy many' prevents differences introduced by rebuilding (dependency or tool version changes). Environment differences come from publish profiles.

example.en: actions/upload-artifact → actions/download-artifact across jobs.

explanation.en: FakeTable isolates the table; AssertEquals verifies the result and fails the test otherwise. The other choices aren't tSQLt procedures for these purposes.

example.en: tSQLt.AssertEqualsTable compares whole result tables.

text.en: Which three are protection rules available on GitHub deployment environments? (Select 3)

explanation.en: Environments support required reviewers, wait timers and restricting which branches/tags can deploy (plus custom protection rules). Backups and Query Store are database features.

example.en: Only main may deploy to production; 15-minute wait; 2 reviewers.

text.en: A deployment to a registered production database is blocked with a drift message. Which publish property caused this?

explanation.en: BlockWhenDriftDetected stops updates to a registered database whose schema no longer matches its registration. Investigate the drift, back-port or accept, then redeploy.

example.en: /p:BlockWhenDriftDetected=False only after deliberately deciding to overwrite drift.

text.en: Match each trigger to its typical pipeline use.
Manual run, e.g. re-deploy or hotfix
Nightly drift checks or long integration tests

explanation.en: Triggers define when pipeline stages run; combining them gives validation, continuous deployment, manual control and periodic checks.

example.en: on: { schedule: [ { cron: '0 2 * * *' } ] }

text.en: Integration tests need a clean SQL Server per pipeline run. Which approach is common on GitHub-hosted Linux runners?
Run a SQL Server container as a job service, publish the dacpac, run tests
Install SQL Server manually each time on Windows

explanation.en: Containers provide disposable, consistent databases; the job publishes the build artifact and runs tests. Production testing is unsafe.

example.en: services: { mssql: { image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest, env: { ACCEPT_EULA: Y, MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TEST_SA }} }, ports: ['1433:1433'] } }

text.en: Which tool visually compares a SQL project with a live database to find drift interactively?

explanation.en: Schema compare lists differences and can apply them in either direction (update project or database). The others are performance/monitoring tools.

example.en: VS Code: right-click project → Schema Compare.

text.en: For each statement about tSQLt, answer Yes or No.
Each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back afterward.
Tests are written as stored procedures in test classes (schemas).
tSQLt should be installed in production databases.

explanation.en: tSQLt isolates tests via rollback and organizes them by schema. It's a development/test dependency — keep it out of production deployments.

example.en: Keep tests in a separate project that references the main project.

text.en: A deployment script contains a table rebuild (create new table, copy data, swap) for a 2-TB table because a column was inserted in the middle of the definition. How should the team avoid this?
Add new columns at the end, or set IgnoreColumnOrder = true in the publish profile so column order changes don't force rebuilds

explanation.en: Column order matters to DacFx comparisons; inserting a column mid-definition can trigger a full rebuild. IgnoreColumnOrder avoids that. Reviewing generated scripts in PRs catches it early.

example.en: /p:IgnoreColumnOrder=True

text.en: Which deployment-test practice best catches post-deployment script failures caused by real data before production?
Publish to a staging copy of production data first
Only run unit tests with fakes

explanation.en: Realistic data reveals constraint violations, data-loss blocks and long operations that empty test databases hide.

example.en: Refresh staging from a masked production copy regularly.

text.en: Complete the CODEOWNERS file so security objects need the security team's review.

explanation.en: The file is named CODEOWNERS (in .github/, root or docs/). Owners are @user or @org/team handles. Later matching lines take precedence, so the Security folder maps to the security team.

example.en: Enable 'Require review from Code Owners' in branch protection.

text.en: In CODEOWNERS, when two patterns match the same file, which owner applies?
The last matching pattern in the file

explanation.en: CODEOWNERS uses last-match-wins precedence, so specific rules go below general ones.

example.en: General /src/Database/ first, specific /src/Database/Security/ after.

text.en: Which two are ways to detect schema drift? (Select 2)
SqlPackage DriftReport against a registered database
Schema compare between the project and the live database

explanation.en: Both compare expected vs actual schema. Wait stats and index maintenance don't reveal schema differences.

example.en: Nightly drift workflow posts results to the team channel.

text.en: Which job setting makes a GitHub Actions job wait for another job's success before running?

explanation.en: needs defines job dependencies, creating stages like build → test → deploy. The other keys aren't valid.

example.en: deploy-prod: { needs: deploy-test, environment: production }

text.en: A production environment restricts deployments to the main branch and requires two reviewers. Answer Yes or No.
A job from a feature branch targeting production is blocked.
Environment secrets become available to the job only after approval.
Reviewers can approve their own deployment unless self-review is prevented.

explanation.en: Branch restrictions block other branches; secrets are released after protection rules pass; GitHub provides a 'Prevent self-review' option — without it, a required reviewer could approve their own run.

example.en: Enable 'Prevent self-review' for separation of duties.

text.en: Which statement about testing RLS predicates is best practice?
Integration-test them by executing queries as different users/session contexts and asserting visible rows
Don't test security; trust the code review

explanation.en: Security logic is behavior worth testing. Testing as an owner (who may bypass) or with RLS disabled proves nothing.

example.en: EXECUTE AS USER = 'tenantA_user'; assert counts; REVERT;

text.en: Order a safe production deployment job.
Publish the tested dacpac with the production profile
Run smoke tests and record the deployment (commit SHA)

explanation.en: Gate, check drift/impact, deploy, verify and record. Skipping the pre-check risks overwriting hotfixes or surprising rebuilds.

example.en: Fail the job if the DeployReport contains unexpected drops.

text.en: What permissions should the database identity used by the production deployment pipeline have?
Only what deployments need (e.g. schema change permissions on the target database), not server-wide sysadmin
The same login as end users

explanation.en: Least privilege applies to automation too. A compromised pipeline with sysadmin could do far more damage. End-user logins shouldn't deploy schemas.

example.en: A dedicated Entra identity added to db_owner on the target database only (or narrower roles).

text.en: Which artifact should a PR pipeline publish for reviewers to inspect the impact of a schema change?
The generated deployment script or DeployReport

explanation.en: The script/report shows exactly what will run against the target, which is what reviewers need.

example.en: actions/upload-artifact with deploy.sql

text.en: A test project contains tSQLt tests. How should it relate to the main database project?
Separate test project referencing the main project (same-database reference), deployed only to test environments
Mixed into the main project and deployed to production

explanation.en: Separating tests keeps production clean while letting tests validate the same model. Tests on laptops aren't automated; post-deployment scripts run in production.

example.en: Sales.sqlproj + Sales.Tests.sqlproj (references Sales).

text.en: Match each control to the risk it mitigates.
Merging code that doesn't build or fails tests
Pipelines using long-lived stored credentials or reaching the wrong environment

explanation.en: These four controls map to the study guide's 'controls for deployment pipelines' bullet: branching policies, approvals, authentication and code owners.

example.en: Layer them for defense in depth.

text.en: How should a failed production deployment be rolled back in a declarative SQL project workflow?
Fix forward or redeploy the previous dacpac version — mindful that data changes may not be reversible
Rollback is automatic for all changes

explanation.en: Publishing the previous version computes changes back, but dropped data can't be recovered by schema deployment; backups/point-in-time restore cover worst cases. Prefer backward-compatible changes so fix-forward is easy.

example.en: Azure SQL point-in-time restore for catastrophic failures.

text.en: Answer Yes or No about testing strategy.
Fast unit tests should run on every pull request.
Integration tests can run on merge or on a schedule if they're slow.
Testing against production data copies requires attention to masking/privacy.

explanation.en: A layered strategy balances feedback speed and coverage; using production data in lower environments requires masking or anonymization.

example.en: PR: build + tSQLt (2 min). Merge: container integration tests (10 min). Nightly: staging deployment test.

text.en: Which tSQLt assertion compares two tables' contents row by row?

explanation.en: AssertEqualsTable compares an expected table to an actual one. AssertEquals compares scalars, Fail forces failure, SpyProcedure replaces a procedure to record calls.

example.en: EXEC tSQLt.AssertEqualsTable 'expected', 'actual';

text.en: A procedure calls dbo.SendEmail internally. In a unit test you want to verify it's called without sending email. Which tSQLt feature?
tSQLt.SpyProcedure on dbo.SendEmail, then check the spy's log table

explanation.en: SpyProcedure replaces the procedure with a stub that logs calls and parameters into a _SpyProcedureLog table. FakeTable works on tables, not procedures.

example.en: EXEC tSQLt.SpyProcedure 'dbo.SendEmail'; … SELECT * FROM dbo.SendEmail_SpyProcedureLog;

text.en: Which two branch-protection settings most directly prevent untested schema changes reaching main? (Select 2)
Require a pull request before merging

explanation.en: PRs plus required checks ensure every change is reviewed and validated. Force pushes and broad bypass undermine protection.

example.en: Rulesets can apply the same rules to many repositories.

text.en: Your deployment must not proceed if the DeployReport shows any DROP TABLE operations. How can the pipeline enforce this?
Generate the DeployReport, parse it in a step, and fail the job if drop operations appear (in addition to BlockOnPossibleDataLoss)

explanation.en: Automated policy checks on the report turn reviews into enforced gates; BlockOnPossibleDataLoss also helps for data-bearing objects.

example.en: grep -q 'Operation Name="Drop"' report.xml && exit 1

text.en: Complete the job so production deployment waits for test deployment and approval.

explanation.en: needs orders jobs; environment links the job to protection rules and environment secrets. The alternatives aren't GitHub Actions keys.

example.en: The job pauses with 'Waiting for review' until approvers act.

text.en: What's a key benefit of running database unit tests in CI on every PR?
Logic regressions in procedures/functions are caught before merge
It removes the need for code review

explanation.en: Early feedback on logic is the point; unit tests complement but don't replace integration tests or reviews.

example.en: Failed tSQLt test → PR status check red → merge blocked.

text.en: Answer Yes or No about drift.
Drift can be caused by manual hotfixes in production.
Ignoring drift can cause a deployment to remove production hotfixes.
Drift is impossible if you use SQL projects.

explanation.en: Projects define intended state, but nothing stops out-of-band changes — detection and process discipline are needed.

example.en: Restrict ALTER permissions in production to the pipeline identity to reduce drift.

text.en: To reduce drift at its source, which permission strategy is most effective in production?
Only the deployment pipeline identity has DDL permissions; humans use break-glass access that's audited
Allow schema changes from any app

explanation.en: If only the pipeline can change schema, all changes flow through source control. Emergency access remains possible but audited.

example.en: Audit SCHEMA_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUP to detect any out-of-band DDL.

text.en: Order the steps of a tSQLt test (Arrange-Act-Assert).

explanation.en: Isolate, arrange data, act, assert — the transaction rolls back afterward automatically.

example.en: FakeTable → INSERT → EXEC proc → AssertEqualsTable.

text.en: In azure/sql-action, how do you pass SqlPackage options such as a publish profile?

explanation.en: The action forwards arguments to SqlPackage, letting you use profiles and /p: properties.

example.en: arguments: '/Profile:prod.publish.xml /p:BlockOnPossibleDataLoss=true'

text.en: Why add a wait timer to a production environment?
To give time to cancel a deployment or observe earlier stages before production proceeds

explanation.en: Wait timers delay deployment jobs, enabling a bake period (e.g. monitor staging) and last-minute cancellation.

example.en: 30-minute wait after staging deployment before production.

text.en: Which two practices make database deployments safer to automate continuously? (Select 2)

explanation.en: Compatible changes let app and DB deploy independently; idempotent scripts make reruns safe. Disabling data-loss protection and per-environment builds add risk.

example.en: Expand → migrate → contract across releases.

text.en: What should happen in CI when the SQL project build reports an unresolved reference?
The check fails and blocks the PR until fixed

explanation.en: Build validation is the first quality gate; failing fast prevents broken schemas from merging.

example.en: Required status check: 'dotnet build Sales.sqlproj'.

text.en: Is each a pipeline control named or implied by the study guide's deployment-controls bullet? Answer Yes or No.

explanation.en: The bullet lists branching policies, triggers in approvals, authentication and code owners — governance controls, not cosmetic settings.

example.en: Map each to a GitHub feature: rulesets, environments, OIDC, CODEOWNERS.

text.en: A hotfix must reach production quickly but still follow controls. What's the best process?
Hotfix branch → PR with expedited review → same pipeline (possibly shorter wait) → production approval
Edit production directly and forget it
Disable branch protection temporarily for everyone
Email the script to the DBA

explanation.en: Even urgent changes should flow through source control and the pipeline, keeping traceability and avoiding drift.

example.en: workflow_dispatch with a 'hotfix' input can skip non-essential stages.

text.en: Which statement about smoke tests after deployment is correct?
Quick checks (e.g. key procedures execute, sample queries return expected shapes) confirm the deployment works

explanation.en: Smoke tests are fast, low-impact sanity checks after deployment; they complement earlier test layers.

example.en: EXEC dbo.HealthCheck; SELECT TOP (1) 1 FROM dbo.Orders;

text.en: Integration tests pass in CI, but production deployment fails because a post-deployment MERGE violates a foreign key on existing data. Which test layer was missing?
A deployment test against production-like data (staging copy)

explanation.en: Empty or synthetic CI databases don't contain production's data quirks. Rehearsing the deployment against realistic data catches these failures. FakeTable removes constraints, so it can't catch FK issues.

example.en: Nightly: restore masked prod → publish → run post-deployment → report.

text.en: Match each test type to what it best detects.
Logic errors in a single procedure/function
Objects working together after a full deployment
Data-dependent deployment failures and long operations
The production deployment is basically healthy

explanation.en: A layered testing strategy assigns each risk to the cheapest test that can catch it.

example.en: The 'testing strategy, including unit tests and integration tests' bullet in practice.
